text:
maria: Quick thread: noticed two prefixes got split during a rolling handoff and ownership convergence lagged, which led to duplicate evictions and a brief availability wobble. Dumping notes and a sketch for discussion.

raj: can you paste logs? was it deterministic after split?

maria: here's a minimal log snippet we captured in staging:
```
[splitter] prefix=a1 -> a1.0,a1.1; old_owner=host-3 new_owner=host-7
[meta_write] host-3 wrote local prefix meta (epoch=42, token=xYz)
[handoff_rpc] sent to host-7, ack delayed 12s (timeout retried)
[evict] host-3 eviction-run: evict prefix=a1.0 (tenant=acme)
[prefetch] host-7 started serving, didn't see pin -> later evict attempt
```

sasha: So sequence looks like: local meta write -> RPC delayed -> eviction path runs on old owner (or still thinks it's owner) -> new owner doesn't see the pin and can also evict. Did healthcheck flip leader around the same time?

maria: healthcheck was green. I think root cause is our ownership marker write ordering: we persist local marker then fire handoff RPC. If RPC is delayed/lost, both sides may think they own parts of the space for a short window. Eviction uses only local marker + lease TTL today.

tess: Possible quick fixes: 1) make ownership commit more atomic (global marker first, or two-phase commit) 2) add a short grace/window where the old owner refuses to evict post-split unless explicit tombstone or confirmation. Tradeoffs?

raj: 2 is the cheapest and low-risk but increases stale residency and can bloat hotset; 1 adds coordination (latency) but gives stronger safety.

jonathan: We could reuse lease epochs: bump epoch on split and require eviction to check epoch equality against in-meta epoch. That avoids extra RPCs during eviction path.

sasha: Epoch check is neat. Need to ensure epoch monotonicity across splits+merges and that epoch reads are cheap. Also we should add metrics to observe grace-window stacking.

maria: Another variant: write a short-lived `split_token` into prefix metadata; evictors must see matching token to proceed. If token mismatch, skip evict for a short TTL.

tess: Edge case: process crash after split before token persisted -> both think owner. Combining token+epoch might be safer.

raj: :thumbsup: can someone sketch a minimal proto and eviction pseudo-code?

maria: Sketch:
```
message PrefixMeta { uint64 epoch; string split_token; int64 token_ts; }
On split: epoch++, generate token, write meta (persist) then RPC handoff.
Eviction: read meta; if local_epoch != meta.epoch || (now - meta.token_ts) < GRACE_MS -> skip evict
// if skip, schedule re-check later or require explicit tombstone before final eviction
```

jonathan: Also emit metrics: `evict_skipped_due_to_epoch_mismatch` and `evict_skipped_due_to_split_token` so ops can tune GRACE_MS.

sasha: How long should GRACE_MS be? 5s? 30s? depends on RPC var latency and our tail latencies.

tess: Start conservative: 10s default. Use histograms to tune per-cluster. Also add a debug endpoint to force full metadata sync for a prefix and bypass grace (for emergency ops).

maria: Plan: I'll open a short RFC + spike PR implementing epoch+token approach behind a feature flag. Default GRACE_MS=10000, add smoke tests for split+delayed-ack and split+crash.

raj: Please add a smoke test that simulates delayed ack and asserts we don't double-evict (or if we do, it's only a single controlled path).

maria: Yep — adding to `kv-integ` suite. Also will add a rate-limited log when eviction is skipped to avoid log spam.

cachebot: deploy-bot: canary deployed split-token spike to staging (rev 6f3b).

jonathan: Nice. Also make eviction skip logs throttled and include prefix id + sample of recent handoff durations for context.

maria: Good call — rate-limit to 1 log per 10s per prefix and include `last_handoff_delay_ms` in log.

tess: Follow-up item: instrument cost impact — short extra residency increases tokens billed. We should add `extra_residency_tokens` metric for reconciliation.

maria: noted, will surface in RFC.

raj: OK, ping when RFC+PR are up and we'll review. Thanks all for quick triage.
